summary: I sent the exact prompt from the story. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, found the vendored Keel kit on its own and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The plan's page code builds the page from the kit: dataTable, selectField, filterBar, badge, emptyState and pageHeader. It does not copy the hand-written markup from services.js. No tracked files were changed. The agent asked no clarifying questions.
reasoning: All four criteria pass. I checked each one against the plan file on disk, the session log's tool calls and git status, not the screen alone. The agent found the unused kit without any hint from me and based the page on dataTable and selectField. It also did not change any tracked files in the repo.

observations.description: To check the plan, the agent cloned the repo into a temporary directory, applied the plan's code and ran the full test suite (it reported 392 tests, 0 failures). The working repo was left untouched, but this goes well beyond writing a plan. The user's "don't start implementing" request was technically respected; reviewers may want to decide whether running the code in a scratch copy is acceptable.
Claude Code's first-run screens ("trust this folder" and the bypass-permissions warning) have "No, exit" selected by default. Pressing Enter without thinking would end the session.

The agent added a long block about installing the Codex plugin, with four slash commands, and said it logged the skipped Codex review to a hyperpowers review log by running a script in the plugin directory. This is noise for a user who only asked for a plan.

The agent's closing summary is clear. It lists the choices the spec left open: chip colors, default sort direction per column, time format, and the empty message for "All environments". It also notes that the e2e fixtures need deploys.json because those tests visit every nav link.
The plan was written to docs/hyperpowers/plans/, which .gitignore ignores, so `git status` does not show it. A user looking for the new file there would not find it.

criteria.evidence: The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". The first tool_use in the session log is "Skill hyperpowers:writing-plans".

criteria.criterion: A plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/ or docs/superpowers/plans/
The plan's page code builds the table and the environment filter with the kit's dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written <table> or <select>
criteria.evidence: The plan's Step 3 code for src/pages/deploys.js imports `selectField` from '#kit/select' and `dataTable` from '#kit/table'. It calls `filterBar({... fields: [selectField({ name: 'env', ...})]})` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: [...], rows: deploys, sort: ..., empty: emptyState(...) })`. The only `<table` in the plan is a test assertion, `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)`, which checks the empty state. Architecture line 9 says it "does not hand-write the HTML the way src/pages/services.js does".

criteria.criterion: The agent did not start implementing: no source, test, data, public, vendor, pipeline, tool or script file, and not package.json, was created or changed
criteria.evidence: After the run, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | wc -l` returned 0, and HEAD is still eb658e0. The plan file does not appear in git status because docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored (`git check-ignore` returned ".gitignore:2:docs/hyperpowers/"). The session log shows Write/Edit calls only on the plan file. The agent's test runs of the plan used `git clone` into a `mktemp -d` directory outside the repo.
